function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

   16| # str.splitlines() method).

   19| # and splits on that basis. The post-processing step puts those back together
   20| # into the actual lines of SQL.

   23|  (?:                     # Start of non-capturing group
   24|   (?:\r\n|\r|\n)      |  # Match any single newline, or
   25|   [^\r\n'"]+          |  # Match any character series without quotes or
   26|                          # newlines, or
   27|   "(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"   |  # Match double-quoted strings, or
   28|   '(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'      # Match single quoted strings

   30| )
   31| """, re.VERBOSE)

   40|     character is inside of a string."""

   67|     :return: function

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

message.content: Based on analysis, the regression is in `_process_identifierlist`'s non-VALUES branch: it used to always split each identifier onto its own line (aligned under the first identifier via `num_offset`), with `wrap_after` only raising the threshold. A later change ("Wrap function params when wrap_after is set") replaced the offset with `adjusted_offset` unconditionally and gated the split condition behind `wrap_after > 0`, which silently disabled the default splitting behavior (since default `wrap_after=0`). I'll restore `num_offset`-based indentation and the always-active split condition, while preserving the function-param-wrap enhancement as an alternate offset chosen only when it actually triggers, and restoring `comma_first` handling in this branch (matching the VALUES branch pattern).

    4| Notable Changes
    5| 
    6| * Drop support for Python 3.8 and 3.9. Python 3.10+ is now required.

    9| 
   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

The regression was in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py). A prior change for wrapping function params replaced the correct per-identifier indentation offset (`num_offset`, aligning continuation lines under the first identifier) with an offset that was 0 whenever the function-wrap case didn't apply, and gated the newline-insertion condition behind `wrap_after > 0` (so with default `wrap_after=0`, identifier lists were never split across lines at all, collapsing e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` formatting).

Fix applied: restore `num_offset` as the base offset (only overridden by the negative `adjusted_offset` when the function-wrap case actually triggers), and restore the original always-active wrap condition `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)` (which naturally triggers wrapping for every comma when `wrap_after` is 0, and only wraps past the threshold when `wrap_after` is set), plus restored `comma_first` handling in this branch matching the VALUES branch.

Verified manually via `python -c ...`:
- `select foo, bar, baz` -> `select foo,\n       bar,\n       baz` (correct alignment under `select `)
- `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `wrap_after=30` on long numeric list still wraps at the right point
- function-param wrap_after case (`select foo(1,2,...)`) still wraps with proper offset
- `where`/`and` clause reindent unaffected
- VALUES clause and comment-in-list cases unaffected

No test directory exists in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be supplied separately), so verification was done via direct `sqlparse.format` calls reproducing the previously-passing behaviors described in the bug report.

message.content:
The regression was in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py). A prior change for wrapping function params replaced the correct per-identifier indentation offset (`num_offset`, aligning continuation lines under the first identifier) with an offset that was 0 whenever the function-wrap case didn't apply, and gated the newline-insertion condition behind `wrap_after > 0` (so with default `wrap_after=0`, identifier lists were never split across lines at all, collapsing e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` formatting).

Fix applied: restore `num_offset` as the base offset (only overridden by the negative `adjusted_offset` when the function-wrap case actually triggers), and restore the original always-active wrap condition `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)` (which naturally triggers wrapping for every comma when `wrap_after` is 0, and only wraps past the threshold when `wrap_after` is set), plus restored `comma_first` handling in this branch matching the VALUES branch.

Verified manually via `python -c ...`:
- `select foo, bar, baz` -> `select foo,\n       bar,\n       baz` (correct alignment under `select `)
- `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `wrap_after=30` on long numeric list still wraps at the right point
- function-param wrap_after case (`select foo(1,2,...)`) still wraps with proper offset
- `where`/`and` clause reindent unaffected
- VALUES clause and comment-in-list cases unaffected

No test directory exists in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be supplied separately), so verification was done via direct `sqlparse.format` calls reproducing the previously-passing behaviors described in the bug report.

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

Based on analysis, the regression is in `_process_identifierlist`'s non-VALUES branch: it used to always split each identifier onto its own line (aligned under the first identifier via `num_offset`), with `wrap_after` only raising the threshold. A later change ("Wrap function params when wrap_after is set") replaced the offset with `adjusted_offset` unconditionally and gated the split condition behind `wrap_after > 0`, which silently disabled the default splitting behavior (since default `wrap_after=0`). I'll restore `num_offset`-based indentation and the always-active split condition, while preserving the function-param-wrap enhancement as an alternate offset chosen only when it actually triggers, and restoring `comma_first` handling in this branch (matching the VALUES branch pattern).

The regression was in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py). A prior change for wrapping function params replaced the correct per-identifier indentation offset (`num_offset`, aligning continuation lines under the first identifier) with an offset that was 0 whenever the function-wrap case didn't apply, and gated the newline-insertion condition behind `wrap_after > 0` (so with default `wrap_after=0`, identifier lists were never split across lines at all, collapsing e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` formatting).

- `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `wrap_after=30` on long numeric list still wraps at the right point
- function-param wrap_after case (`select foo(1,2,...)`) still wraps with proper offset
- `where`/`and` clause reindent unaffected
- VALUES clause and comment-in-list cases unaffected

A prior change for wrapping function params replaced the correct per-identifier indentation offset (`num_offset`, aligning continuation lines under the first identifier) with an offset that was 0 whenever the function-wrap case didn't apply, and gated the newline-insertion condition behind `wrap_after > 0` (so with default `wrap_after=0`, identifier lists were never split across lines at all, collapsing e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` formatting).

- `wrap_after=30` on long numeric list still wraps at the right point
- function-param wrap_after case (`select foo(1,2,...)`) still wraps with proper offset
- `where`/`and` clause reindent unaffected

Root cause: in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py), the non-VALUES/non-comma-in-function branch that handles ordinary `SELECT col1, col2, ...` identifier lists had been rewritten to support the newer "wrap function params" feature. That rewrite (a) always used `offset(self, adjusted_offset)` where `adjusted_offset` is 0 unless the specific function-wrap heuristic triggers — discarding the previously-computed `num_offset` (the column under which continuation lines should align), and (b) gated the newline-insertion condition behind `self.wrap_after > 0`, so with the default `wrap_after=0` no line breaks were ever inserted for identifier lists at all. This silently disabled reindenting of ordinary column/identifier lists (e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` stayed on one line, `where` clauses following them lost their expected formatting context, etc.), matching the reported regression across ~15 reindent tests.

Fix: restored `num_offset` as the offset used for this branch (falling back to the function-wrap `adjusted_offset` only when that heuristic actually applies, i.e. is negative), and restored the always-active wrap condition `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)` (which naturally triggers on every comma when `wrap_after` is 0, matching original/expected behavior, and only wraps past the threshold when `wrap_after` is set) together with the `comma_first` handling, mirroring the sibling VALUES-branch logic. Also dropped the now-superfluous `indent(self)` context manager in this branch since `num_offset`/`adjusted_offset` are already absolute column offsets (consistent with how the VALUES branch computes its offset).

Verified via manual `sqlparse.format` calls:
- `select foo, bar, baz` -> `select foo,\n       bar,\n       baz`
- with `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `select foo, bar, baz from table1 where 1 = 2` -> proper multi-line output with `where`/`and` clauses aligned
- `wrap_after=30` on a long identifier list wraps at the correct column
- function-param wrap-after case (`select foo(1,2,...)` with `wrap_after`) still wraps using the function-offset heuristic
- VALUES clause formatting and comment-in-list formatting remain unaffected

No local test suite is present in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be run separately), so correctness was confirmed by directly reproducing the previously-passing formatting behaviors described in the bug report.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

   10| Security Fixes
   11| 
   12| * Fix uncontrolled CPU consumption in ``TokenList`` grouping (CWE-1333,
   13|   patches by alhudz and tonghuaroot, pr848).  Two independent
   14|   quadratic behaviours were fixed:
   15| 
   16|   - ``TokenList.__init__`` called ``str(self)`` which recursively flattened
   17|     the entire token subtree on every group construction.  Deeply nested SQL
   18|     (parentheses, CASE WHEN, subqueries) therefore costs O(n·depth) CPU
   19|     before the depth cap fires — a ~2 KB payload could pin a worker for 10+
   20|     seconds.  Fix: join children's already-cached ``value`` fields directly,
   21|     reducing per-node cost to O(len(tokens)).
   22| 
   23|   - ``group_tokens()`` recomputed ``grp.value = str(start)`` on every extend
   24|     step, re-scanning the entire growing group each time.  Wide flat queries
   25|     (e.g. SELECT with thousands of columns) therefore cost O(N²) in the
   26|     number of columns.  Fix: append only the newly added tokens' values.

Based on analysis, the regression is in `_process_identifierlist`'s non-VALUES branch: it used to always split each identifier onto its own line (aligned under the first identifier via `num_offset`), with `wrap_after` only raising the threshold. A later change ("Wrap function params when wrap_after is set") replaced the offset with `adjusted_offset` unconditionally and gated the split condition behind `wrap_after > 0`, which silently disabled the default splitting behavior (since default `wrap_after=0`). I'll restore `num_offset`-based indentation and the always-active split condition, while preserving the function-param-wrap enhancement as an alternate offset chosen only when it actually triggers, and restoring `comma_first` handling in this branch (matching the VALUES branch pattern).

Root cause: in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py), the non-VALUES/non-comma-in-function branch that handles ordinary `SELECT col1, col2, ...` identifier lists had been rewritten to support the newer "wrap function params" feature. That rewrite (a) always used `offset(self, adjusted_offset)` where `adjusted_offset` is 0 unless the specific function-wrap heuristic triggers — discarding the previously-computed `num_offset` (the column under which continuation lines should align), and (b) gated the newline-insertion condition behind `self.wrap_after > 0`, so with the default `wrap_after=0` no line breaks were ever inserted for identifier lists at all. This silently disabled reindenting of ordinary column/identifier lists (e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` stayed on one line, `where` clauses following them lost their expected formatting context, etc.), matching the reported regression across ~15 reindent tests.

Fix: restored `num_offset` as the offset used for this branch (falling back to the function-wrap `adjusted_offset` only when that heuristic actually applies, i.e. is negative), and restored the always-active wrap condition `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)` (which naturally triggers on every comma when `wrap_after` is 0, matching original/expected behavior, and only wraps past the threshold when `wrap_after` is set) together with the `comma_first` handling, mirroring the sibling VALUES-branch logic. Also dropped the now-superfluous `indent(self)` context manager in this branch since `num_offset`/`adjusted_offset` are already absolute column offsets (consistent with how the VALUES branch computes its offset).

Verified via manual `sqlparse.format` calls:
- `select foo, bar, baz` -> `select foo,\n       bar,\n       baz`
- with `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `select foo, bar, baz from table1 where 1 = 2` -> proper multi-line output with `where`/`and` clauses aligned
- `wrap_after=30` on a long identifier list wraps at the correct column
- function-param wrap-after case (`select foo(1,2,...)` with `wrap_after`) still wraps using the function-offset heuristic
- VALUES clause formatting and comment-in-list formatting remain unaffected

No local test suite is present in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be run separately), so correctness was confirmed by directly reproducing the previously-passing formatting behaviors described in the bug report.

- `wrap_after=30` on long numeric list still wraps at the right point
- function-param wrap_after case (`select foo(1,2,...)`) still wraps with proper offset
- `where`/`and` clause reindent unaffected

Root cause: in `_process_identifierlist` (sqlparse/filters/reindent.py), the non-VALUES/non-comma-in-function branch that handles ordinary `SELECT col1, col2, ...` identifier lists had been rewritten to support the newer "wrap function params" feature. That rewrite (a) always used `offset(self, adjusted_offset)` where `adjusted_offset` is 0 unless the specific function-wrap heuristic triggers — discarding the previously-computed `num_offset` (the column under which continuation lines should align), and (b) gated the newline-insertion condition behind `self.wrap_after > 0`, so with the default `wrap_after=0` no line breaks were ever inserted for identifier lists at all. This silently disabled reindenting of ordinary column/identifier lists (e.g. `select foo, bar, baz` stayed on one line, `where` clauses following them lost their expected formatting context, etc.), matching the reported regression across ~15 reindent tests.

Fix: restored `num_offset` as the offset used for this branch (falling back to the function-wrap `adjusted_offset` only when that heuristic actually applies, i.e. is negative), and restored the always-active wrap condition `position > (self.wrap_after - self.offset)` (which naturally triggers on every comma when `wrap_after` is 0, matching original/expected behavior, and only wraps past the threshold when `wrap_after` is set) together with the `comma_first` handling, mirroring the sibling VALUES-branch logic. Also dropped the now-superfluous `indent(self)` context manager in this branch since `num_offset`/`adjusted_offset` are already absolute column offsets (consistent with how the VALUES branch computes its offset).

Verified via manual `sqlparse.format` calls:
- `select foo, bar, baz` -> `select foo,\n       bar,\n       baz`
- with `comma_first=True` -> `select foo\n     , bar\n     , baz`
- `select foo, bar, baz from table1 where 1 = 2` -> proper multi-line output with `where`/`and` clauses aligned
- `wrap_after=30` on a long identifier list wraps at the correct column
- function-param wrap-after case (`select foo(1,2,...)` with `wrap_after`) still wraps using the function-offset heuristic
- VALUES clause formatting and comment-in-list formatting remain unaffected

No local test suite is present in this checkout (hidden upstream tests will be run separately), so correctness was confirmed by directly reproducing the previously-passing formatting behaviors described in the bug report.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.
